statement.text:
Suppose α is an endomorphism of a group G such that for every group H
and every homomorphism f : G → H, there exists an endomorphism βf of H such
that βf f = f α. Must α then be either an inner automorphism of G or the trivial
endomorphism? This is Question 5 in (G. M. Bergman, Publ. Matem., 56 (2012),
91–126).                                                         G. M. Bergman
  ∗ Yes, it must (F. Fournier-Facio, Preprint, 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.
05728)
